# hermes
## HarnessBench adapter
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from harnessbench.adapters.base import BaseAdapter
from harnessbench.models import AdapterRunContext, AdapterRunResult
from harnessbench.usage_proxy import register_routes


def _project_root() -> Path:
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def _resolve_project_path(raw: str | Path) -> Path:
    path = Path(os.path.expanduser(str(raw)))
    if not path.is_absolute():
        path = _project_root() / path
    return path.resolve()


def _source_config_from_model_config(model_cfg: dict[str, object]) -> Path:
    raw = model_cfg.get("user_config")
    if raw:
        return _resolve_project_path(str(raw))
    env_raw = os.environ.get("HERMES_CONFIG_PATH") or os.environ.get("HERMES_CONFIG")
    if env_raw:
        return _resolve_project_path(env_raw)
    return _resolve_project_path("~/.hermes/config.yaml")


def _load_yaml(path: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
    try:
        import yaml  # type: ignore
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        try:
            from ruamel import yaml  # type: ignore
        except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError("Hermes adapter requires PyYAML or ruamel.yaml to rewrite config") from exc

    data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return dict(data or {}) if isinstance(data, dict) else {}


def _dump_yaml(path: Path, data: dict[str, object]) -> None:
    try:
        import yaml  # type: ignore
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        try:
            from ruamel import yaml  # type: ignore
        except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError("Hermes adapter requires PyYAML or ruamel.yaml to rewrite config") from exc

    path.write_text(
        yaml.safe_dump(data, allow_unicode=True, sort_keys=False),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )


def _safe_name(raw: str, fallback: str) -> str:
    cleaned = "".join(ch if ch.isalnum() or ch in ("-", "_", ".") else "-" for ch in raw).strip("-._")
    return cleaned or fallback


def _register_route(
    routes: dict[str, dict[str, str]],
    *,
    proxy_base_url: str,
    upstream: str,
    route_name: str,
    provider: str,
) -> str:
    prefix = f"/hermes/{route_name}"
    routes[prefix] = {
        "framework": "hermes",
        "provider": provider,
        "upstream": upstream,
    }
    return f"{proxy_base_url}{prefix}"


def _matching_custom_provider(
    custom_providers: object,
    base_url: str,
    model_name: str,
) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    if not isinstance(custom_providers, list) or not base_url:
        return None
    candidates = [
        entry
        for entry in custom_providers
        if isinstance(entry, dict)
        and str(entry.get("base_url") or "").strip().rstrip("/") == base_url
        and str(entry.get("api_key") or "").strip()
    ]
    if not candidates:
        return None
    if model_name:
        for entry in candidates:
            if str(entry.get("model") or "").strip() == model_name:
                return entry
    return candidates[0]


def _merge_user_config(
    user_config: Path,
    out_path: Path,
    *,
    proxy_base_url: str = "",
    proxy_routes_file: Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    data = _load_yaml(user_config)
    routes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    custom_providers = data.get("custom_providers")

    def rewrite_url(raw: object, route_name: str, provider: str) -> str | None:
        upstream = str(raw or "").strip().rstrip("/")
        if not upstream:
            return None
        if proxy_base_url and upstream.startswith(proxy_base_url.rstrip("/")):
            return upstream
        if proxy_base_url and proxy_routes_file is not None:
            return _register_route(
                routes,
                proxy_base_url=proxy_base_url,
                upstream=upstream,
                route_name=route_name,
                provider=provider,
            )
        return upstream

    model_cfg = data.get("model")
    if isinstance(model_cfg, dict):
        provider_name = str(model_cfg.get("provider") or "model").strip() or "model"
        original_base_url = str(model_cfg.get("base_url") or "").strip().rstrip("/")
        model_name = str(model_cfg.get("default") or model_cfg.get("model") or "").strip()
        matching_provider = _matching_custom_provider(custom_providers, original_base_url, model_name)
        if proxy_base_url and matching_provider:
            matching_name = str(matching_provider.get("name") or "custom").strip() or "custom"
            rewritten = _register_route(
                routes,
                proxy_base_url=proxy_base_url,
                upstream=original_base_url,
                route_name=f"custom-{_safe_name(matching_name, 'custom')}",
                provider=matching_name,
            )
        else:
            rewritten = rewrite_url(original_base_url, f"model-{_safe_name(provider_name, 'model')}", provider_name)
        if rewritten:
            if proxy_base_url and matching_provider and not str(model_cfg.get("api_mode") or "").strip():
                api_mode = str(matching_provider.get("api_mode") or "").strip()
                if api_mode:
                    model_cfg["api_mode"] = api_mode
            model_cfg["base_url"] = rewritten

    if isinstance(custom_providers, list):
        for index, entry in enumerate(custom_providers):
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            provider_name = str(entry.get("name") or f"custom-{index}").strip() or f"custom-{index}"
            rewritten = rewrite_url(entry.get("base_url"), f"custom-{_safe_name(provider_name, f'custom-{index}')}", provider_name)
            if rewritten:
                entry["base_url"] = rewritten

    auxiliary = data.get("auxiliary")
    if isinstance(auxiliary, dict):
        for key, entry in auxiliary.items():
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            rewritten = rewrite_url(entry.get("base_url"), f"aux-{_safe_name(str(key), 'aux')}", str(key))
            if rewritten:
                entry["base_url"] = rewritten

    if routes and proxy_routes_file is not None:
        register_routes(proxy_routes_file, routes)

    _dump_yaml(out_path, data)


def _build_command(ctx: AdapterRunContext, command: str, args: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    fmt = {
        "workspace": str(ctx.workspace),
        "sandbox": str(ctx.sandbox),
        "prompt_file": str(ctx.prompt_file),
        "session_id": ctx.session_id,
        "task_id": ctx.task.task_id,
        "model_id": ctx.model_id,
    }
    cmd = [command, *[str(arg).format(**fmt) for arg in args]]

    if "-q" in cmd or "--query" in cmd:
        for index, arg in enumerate(cmd):
            if arg in {"-q", "--query"}:
                cmd.insert(index + 1, ctx.prompt)
                break
        return cmd

    cmd.extend(["-q", ctx.prompt])
    return cmd


# Hermes session ID 格式：YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_xxxxxxxx
# 匹配 stdout/stderr 中 "Session: 20260410_181750_d6f1d7" 这样的行
# 注意：该行被 Unicode 框线字符（│ U+2502）包裹，需要用 re.search 而非 startswith
_SESSION_ID_RE = re.compile(r"Session:\s*(\d{8}_\d{6}_[0-9a-f]+)", re.IGNORECASE)

# Hermes 在多线程退出时会因 CPython stdin buffer lock 竞争而以 SIGABRT(-6) 退出。
# 这是已知的无害 bug，任务本身已完整执行，不应视为失败。
_BENIGN_RETURNCODES = {0, -6}


def _parse_session_id(text: str) -> str | None:
    """从 Hermes stdout/stderr 中提取 session ID。"""
    match = _SESSION_ID_RE.search(text)
    return match.group(1) if match else None


class HermesAgentAdapter(BaseAdapter):
    name = "hermes_agent"

    def run(self, ctx: AdapterRunContext) -> AdapterRunResult:
        command = str(ctx.model_config.get("command") or "hermes")
        args = [str(arg) for arg in (ctx.model_config.get("args") or ["chat"])]
        use_usage_proxy = bool(ctx.model_config.get("use_usage_proxy", False))

        source_config = _source_config_from_model_config(ctx.model_config)
        if not source_config.is_file():
            return AdapterRunResult(ok=False, stderr=f"missing Hermes source config: {source_config}")

        isolated_home = ctx.sandbox
        hermes_home = isolated_home / ".hermes"
        hermes_home.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        hermes_workspace = hermes_home / "workspace"
        hermes_workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        sandbox_user_config = hermes_home / "config.src.yaml"
        shutil.copy2(source_config, sandbox_user_config)
        merged_cfg = hermes_home / "config.yaml"
        _merge_user_config(
            sandbox_user_config,
            merged_cfg,
            proxy_base_url=str(ctx.env.get("HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_URL") or "") if use_usage_proxy else "",
            proxy_routes_file=(
                Path(ctx.env["HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_ROUTES"])
                if use_usage_proxy and ctx.env.get("HARNESSBENCH_LLM_PROXY_ROUTES")
                else None
            ),
        )

        # ── Session 续接逻辑 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
        # 每轮结束后把 Hermes session ID 写入 last_session_id.txt，
        # 下一轮优先用 --resume <id> 续接；若文件不存在（第 1 轮）则不加任何参数。
        # 若上一轮因 stdout 格式问题未能解析到 session ID，则 fallback 到 -c
        # （让 Hermes 自动续接最近一次 session），保证多轮对话上下文连续。
        session_id_file = hermes_home / "last_session_id.txt"
        resume_session_id: str | None = None
        resume_method: str = "none"  # "resume" | "continue" | "none"

        if session_id_file.exists():
            saved = session_id_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
            if saved:
                resume_session_id = saved
                resume_method = "resume"

        # ── 构建命令 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        cmd = _build_command(ctx, command, args)

        if resume_method == "resume":
            # 精确续接：--resume <session_id>
            cmd.extend(["--resume", resume_session_id])
        elif resume_method == "continue":
            # Fallback：-c 续接最近一次 session（当上一轮 session ID 解析失败时）
            cmd.append("-c")

        # ── 执行 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        env = os.environ.copy()
        env["HOME"] = str(isolated_home)
        env["HERMES_HOME"] = str(hermes_home)
        env["HERMES_CONFIG"] = str(merged_cfg)
        env["HERMES_CONFIG_PATH"] = str(merged_cfg)

        completed = subprocess.run(
            cmd,
            cwd=str(ctx.workspace),
            text=True,
            capture_output=True,
            timeout=ctx.timeout_sec,
            env=env,
            check=False,
        )

        # ── 解析本轮产生的 session ID ─────────────────────────────────────────
        # Hermes 在 stdout 的 UI 框里打印：
        #   │             Session: 20260410_181750_d6f1d7             │
        # 用 re.search 可以穿透框线字符直接匹配。
        combined_output = completed.stdout + "\n" + completed.stderr
        session_id_from_output = _parse_session_id(combined_output)

        # 持久化 session ID 供下一轮使用
        if session_id_from_output:
            # 成功解析：写入精确 ID，下一轮用 --resume
            session_id_file.write_text(session_id_from_output, encoding="utf-8")
        elif resume_session_id:
            # 本轮未解析到新 ID（可能是 Hermes 版本差异），保留上一轮的 ID
            session_id_file.write_text(resume_session_id, encoding="utf-8")
        else:
            # 第 1 轮且未解析到 ID：写入特殊标记，下一轮用 -c fallback
            session_id_file.write_text("__use_continue__", encoding="utf-8")

        # 处理 fallback 标记（上一轮写入了 __use_continue__）
        if resume_session_id == "__use_continue__":
            resume_method = "continue"
            resume_session_id = None

        # ── 判断本轮是否成功 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
        # returncode -6 (SIGABRT) 是 CPython 多线程退出时的已知无害 bug，
        # 只要 stdout 有内容就认为任务执行完成。
        rc = completed.returncode
        if rc in _BENIGN_RETURNCODES:
            ok = bool(completed.stdout.strip())
        else:
            ok = False

        return AdapterRunResult(
            ok=ok,
            command=cmd,
            stdout=completed.stdout,
            stderr=completed.stderr,
            metadata={
                "returncode": rc,
                "source_user_config_path": str(source_config),
                "sandbox_user_config_path": str(sandbox_user_config),
                "hermes_config_path": str(merged_cfg),
                "isolated_home": str(isolated_home),
                "hermes_home": str(hermes_home),
                "hermes_workspace": str(hermes_workspace),
                "workspace": str(ctx.workspace),
                "usage_proxy_enabled": use_usage_proxy,
                "session_id": ctx.session_id,
                "hermes_session_id": session_id_from_output or resume_session_id,
                "resume_method": resume_method,
            },
        )

# Hermes Agent ☤

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Docs-hermes--agent.nousresearch.com-FFD700?style=for-the-badge" alt="Documentation"></a>
  <a href="https://discord.gg/NousResearch"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white" alt="Discord"></a>
  <a href="https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/LICENSE"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green?style=for-the-badge" alt="License: MIT"></a>
  <a href="https://nousresearch.com"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20by-Nous%20Research-blueviolet?style=for-the-badge" alt="Built by Nous Research"></a>
</p>

**The self-improving AI agent built by [Nous Research](https://nousresearch.com).** It's the only agent with a built-in learning loop — it creates skills from experience, improves them during use, nudges itself to persist knowledge, searches its own past conversations, and builds a deepening model of who you are across sessions. Run it on a $5 VPS, a GPU cluster, or serverless infrastructure that costs nearly nothing when idle. It's not tied to your laptop — talk to it from Telegram while it works on a cloud VM.

Use any model you want — [Nous Portal](https://portal.nousresearch.com), [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai) (200+ models), [z.ai/GLM](https://z.ai), [Kimi/Moonshot](https://platform.moonshot.ai), [MiniMax](https://www.minimax.io), OpenAI, or your own endpoint. Switch with `hermes model` — no code changes, no lock-in.

<table>
<tr><td><b>A real terminal interface</b></td><td>Full TUI with multiline editing, slash-command autocomplete, conversation history, interrupt-and-redirect, and streaming tool output.</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Lives where you do</b></td><td>Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, and CLI — all from a single gateway process. Voice memo transcription, cross-platform conversation continuity.</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>A closed learning loop</b></td><td>Agent-curated memory with periodic nudges. Autonomous skill creation after complex tasks. Skills self-improve during use. FTS5 session search with LLM summarization for cross-session recall. <a href="https://github.com/plastic-labs/honcho">Honcho</a> dialectic user modeling. Compatible with the <a href="https://agentskills.io">agentskills.io</a> open standard.</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Scheduled automations</b></td><td>Built-in cron scheduler with delivery to any platform. Daily reports, nightly backups, weekly audits — all in natural language, running unattended.</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Delegates and parallelizes</b></td><td>Spawn isolated subagents for parallel workstreams. Write Python scripts that call tools via RPC, collapsing multi-step pipelines into zero-context-cost turns.</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Runs anywhere, not just your laptop</b></td><td>Six terminal backends — local, Docker, SSH, Daytona, Singularity, and Modal. Daytona and Modal offer serverless persistence — your agent's environment hibernates when idle and wakes on demand, costing nearly nothing between sessions. Run it on a $5 VPS or a GPU cluster.</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>Research-ready</b></td><td>Batch trajectory generation, Atropos RL environments, trajectory compression for training the next generation of tool-calling models.</td></tr>
</table>

## Quick Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

Works on Linux, macOS, WSL2, and Android via Termux. The installer handles the platform-specific setup for you.

> **Android / Termux:** The tested manual path is documented in the [Termux guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/termux). On Termux, Hermes installs a curated `.[termux]` extra because the full `.[all]` extra currently pulls Android-incompatible voice dependencies.
>
> **Windows:** Native Windows is not supported. Please install [WSL2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) and run the command above.

After installation:

```bash
source ~/.bashrc    # reload shell (or: source ~/.zshrc)
hermes              # start chatting!
```

---

## Getting Started

```bash
hermes              # Interactive CLI — start a conversation
hermes model        # Choose your LLM provider and model
hermes tools        # Configure which tools are enabled
hermes config set   # Set individual config values
hermes gateway      # Start the messaging gateway (Telegram, Discord, etc.)
hermes setup        # Run the full setup wizard (configures everything at once)
hermes claw migrate # Migrate from OpenClaw (if coming from OpenClaw)
hermes update       # Update to the latest version
hermes doctor       # Diagnose any issues
```

📖 **[Full documentation →](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/)**

## CLI vs Messaging Quick Reference

Hermes has two entry points: start the terminal UI with `hermes`, or run the gateway and talk to it from Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, or Email. Once you're in a conversation, many slash commands are shared across both interfaces.

| Action | CLI | Messaging platforms |
|---------|-----|---------------------|
| Start chatting | `hermes` | Run `hermes gateway setup` + `hermes gateway start`, then send the bot a message |
| Start fresh conversation | `/new` or `/reset` | `/new` or `/reset` |
| Change model | `/model [provider:model]` | `/model [provider:model]` |
| Set a personality | `/personality [name]` | `/personality [name]` |
| Retry or undo the last turn | `/retry`, `/undo` | `/retry`, `/undo` |
| Compress context / check usage | `/compress`, `/usage`, `/insights [--days N]` | `/compress`, `/usage`, `/insights [days]` |
| Browse skills | `/skills` or `/<skill-name>` | `/skills` or `/<skill-name>` |
| Interrupt current work | `Ctrl+C` or send a new message | `/stop` or send a new message |
| Platform-specific status | `/platforms` | `/status`, `/sethome` |

For the full command lists, see the [CLI guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/cli) and the [Messaging Gateway guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging).

## Migrating from OpenClaw

If you're coming from OpenClaw, Hermes can automatically import your settings, memories, skills, and API keys.

**During first-time setup:** The setup wizard (`hermes setup`) automatically detects `~/.openclaw` and offers to migrate before configuration begins.

**Anytime after install:**

```bash
hermes claw migrate              # Interactive migration (full preset)
hermes claw migrate --dry-run    # Preview what would be migrated
hermes claw migrate --preset user-data   # Migrate without secrets
hermes claw migrate --overwrite  # Overwrite existing conflicts
```

What gets imported:
- **SOUL.md** — persona file
- **Memories** — MEMORY.md and USER.md entries
- **Skills** — user-created skills → `~/.hermes/skills/openclaw-imports/`
- **Command allowlist** — approval patterns
- **Messaging settings** — platform configs, allowed users, working directory
- **API keys** — allowlisted secrets (Telegram, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, ElevenLabs)
- **TTS assets** — workspace audio files
- **Workspace instructions** — AGENTS.md (with `--workspace-target`)

See `hermes claw migrate --help` for all options, or use the `openclaw-migration` skill for an interactive agent-guided migration with dry-run previews.

## Contributing

We welcome contributions! See the [Contributing Guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/contributing) for development setup, code style, and PR process.

Quick start for contributors:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git
cd hermes-agent
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
uv venv venv --python 3.11
source venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[all,dev]"
python -m pytest tests/ -q
```

> **RL Training (optional):** To work on the RL/Tinker-Atropos integration:
> ```bash
> git submodule update --init tinker-atropos
> uv pip install -e "./tinker-atropos"
> ```

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/migration/openclaw.md-112-## Post-Migration Notes

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/migration/openclaw.md:114:- **Skills require a new session** — imported skills take effect after restarting your agent or starting a new chat.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/migration/openclaw.md-115-- **WhatsApp requires re-pairing** — WhatsApp uses QR-code pairing, not token-based auth. Run `hermes whatsapp` to pair.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-57-|---|---|---|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md:58:| `include` | string or list | Whitelist server-native MCP tools |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md:59:| `exclude` | string or list | Blacklist server-native MCP tools |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-60-| `resources` | bool-like | Enable/disable `list_resources` + `read_resource` |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-61-| `prompts` | bool-like | Enable/disable `list_prompts` + `get_prompt` |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-219-### Name sanitization
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-220-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md:221:Hyphens (`-`) and dots (`.`) in both server names and tool names are replaced with underscores before registration. This ensures tool names are valid identifiers for LLM function-calling APIs.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-222-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md:223:For example, a server named `my-api` exposing a tool called `list-items.v2` becomes:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-224-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-225-```text
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-227-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-228-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md:229:Keep this in mind when writing `include` / `exclude` filters — use the **original** MCP tool name (with hyphens/dots), not the sanitized version.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-230-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-231-## OAuth 2.1 authentication
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-242-Behavior:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-243-- Hermes uses the MCP SDK's OAuth 2.1 PKCE flow (metadata discovery, dynamic client registration, token exchange, and refresh)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md:244:- On first connect, a browser window opens for authorization
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md:245:- Tokens are persisted to `~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/<server>.json` and reused across sessions
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-246-- Token refresh is automatic; re-authorization only happens when refresh fails
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md-247-- Only applies to HTTP/StreamableHTTP transport (`url`-based servers)
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/acp-setup.md-3-Hermes Agent supports the **Agent Client Protocol (ACP)**, allowing it to run as
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/acp-setup.md-4-a coding agent inside your editor. ACP lets your IDE send tasks to Hermes, and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/acp-setup.md:5:Hermes responds with file edits, terminal commands, and explanations — all shown
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/acp-setup.md-6-natively in the editor UI.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/acp-setup.md-7-
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/acp-setup.md-20-```

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md-5----
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md-6-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md:7:# Built-in Tools Reference
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md-8-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md:9:This page documents all 47 built-in tools in the Hermes tool registry, grouped by toolset. Availability varies by platform, credentials, and enabled toolsets.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md-10-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md:11:**Quick counts:** 10 browser tools, 4 file tools, 10 RL tools, 4 Home Assistant tools, 2 terminal tools, 2 web tools, and 15 standalone tools across other toolsets.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md-12-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md:13::::tip MCP Tools
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md:14:In addition to built-in tools, Hermes can load tools dynamically from MCP servers. MCP tools appear with a server-name prefix (e.g., `github_create_issue` for the `github` MCP server). See [MCP Integration](/docs/user-guide/features/mcp) for configuration.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md-15-:::

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-7-## Overview
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-8-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:9:Two independent Honcho integrations have been built for two different agent runtimes: **Hermes Agent** (Python, baked into the runner) and **openclaw-honcho** (TypeScript plugin via hook/tool API). Both use the same Honcho peer paradigm — dual peer model, `session.context()`, `peer.chat()` — but they made different tradeoffs at every layer.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-10-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-11-This document maps those tradeoffs and defines a porting spec: a set of Hermes-originated patterns, each stated as an integration-agnostic interface, that any Honcho integration can adopt regardless of runtime or language.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-19-### Hermes: baked-in runner
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-20-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:21:Honcho is initialised directly inside `AIAgent.__init__`. There is no plugin boundary. Session management, context injection, async prefetch, and CLI surface are all first-class concerns of the runner. Context is injected once per session (baked into `_cached_system_prompt`) and never re-fetched mid-session — this maximises prefix cache hits at the LLM provider.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-22-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-23-Turn flow:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-30-  → response
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-31-  → _honcho_fire_prefetch()  (daemon threads, turn end)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:32:       → prefetch_context() thread  ──┐
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:33:       → prefetch_dialectic() thread ─┴→ _context_cache / _dialectic_cache
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-34-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-35-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-36-### openclaw-honcho: hook-based plugin
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-37-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:38:The plugin registers hooks against OpenClaw's event bus. Context is fetched synchronously inside `before_prompt_build` on every turn. Message capture happens in `agent_end`. The multi-agent hierarchy is tracked via `subagent_spawned`. This model is correct but every turn pays a blocking Honcho round-trip before the LLM call can begin.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-39-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-40-Turn flow:
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-43-user message
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-44-  → before_prompt_build (BLOCKING HTTP — every turn)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:45:       → session.context()
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-46-  → system prompt assembled
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-47-  → LLM call
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-48-  → response
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-49-  → agent_end hook
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:50:       → session.addMessages()
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:51:       → session.setMetadata()
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-52-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-53-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-58-| Dimension | Hermes Agent | openclaw-honcho |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-59-|---|---|---|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:60:| **Context injection timing** | Once per session (cached). Zero HTTP on response path after turn 1. | Every turn, blocking. Fresh context per turn but adds latency. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-61-| **Prefetch strategy** | Daemon threads fire at turn end; consumed next turn from cache. | None. Blocking call at prompt-build time. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:62:| **Dialectic (peer.chat)** | Prefetched async; result injected into system prompt next turn. | On-demand via `honcho_recall` / `honcho_analyze` tools. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:63:| **Reasoning level** | Dynamic: scales with message length. Floor = config default. Cap = "high". | Fixed per tool: recall=minimal, analyze=medium. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:64:| **Memory modes** | `user_memory_mode` / `agent_memory_mode`: hybrid / honcho / local. | None. Always writes to Honcho. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:65:| **Write frequency** | async (background queue), turn, session, N turns. | After every agent_end (no control). |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-66-| **AI peer identity** | `observe_me=True`, `seed_ai_identity()`, `get_ai_representation()`, SOUL.md → AI peer. | Agent files uploaded to agent peer at setup. No ongoing self-observation. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:67:| **Context scope** | User peer + AI peer representation, both injected. | User peer (owner) representation + conversation summary. `peerPerspective` on context call. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:68:| **Session naming** | per-directory / global / manual map / title-based. | Derived from platform session key. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:69:| **Multi-agent** | Single-agent only. | Parent observer hierarchy via `subagent_spawned`. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:70:| **Tool surface** | Single `query_user_context` tool (on-demand dialectic). | 6 tools: session, profile, search, context (fast) + recall, analyze (LLM). |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-71-| **Platform metadata** | Not stripped. | Explicitly stripped before Honcho storage. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:72:| **Message dedup** | None. | `lastSavedIndex` in session metadata prevents re-sending. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-73-| **CLI surface in prompt** | Management commands injected into system prompt. Agent knows its own CLI. | Not injected. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-74-| **AI peer name in identity** | Replaces "Hermes Agent" in DEFAULT_AGENT_IDENTITY when configured. | Not implemented. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:75:| **QMD / local file search** | Not implemented. | Passthrough tools when QMD backend configured. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:76:| **Workspace metadata** | Not implemented. | `agentPeerMap` in workspace metadata tracks agent→peer ID. |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-104-### Problem
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-105-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:106:Calling `session.context()` and `peer.chat()` synchronously before each LLM call adds 200–800ms of Honcho round-trip latency to every turn.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-107-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-108-### Pattern
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-109-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:110:Fire both calls as non-blocking background work at the **end** of each turn. Store results in a per-session cache keyed by session ID. At the **start** of the next turn, pop from cache — the HTTP is already done. First turn is cold (empty cache); all subsequent turns are zero-latency on the response path.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-111-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-112-### Interface contract
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-114-```typescript
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-115-interface AsyncPrefetch {
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:116:  // Fire context + dialectic fetches at turn end. Non-blocking.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:117:  firePrefetch(sessionId: string, userMessage: string): void;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-118-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-119-  // Pop cached results at turn start. Returns empty if cache is cold.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:120:  popContextResult(sessionId: string): ContextResult | null;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:121:  popDialecticResult(sessionId: string): string | null;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-122-}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-123-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:124:type ContextResult = {
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-125-  representation: string;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-126-  card: string[];
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:127:  aiRepresentation?: string;  // AI peer context if enabled
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-128-  summary?: string;           // conversation summary if fetched
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-129-};
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-132-### Implementation notes
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-133-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:134:- **Python:** `threading.Thread(daemon=True)`. Write to `dict[session_id, result]` — GIL makes this safe for simple writes.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:135:- **TypeScript:** `Promise` stored in `Map<string, Promise<ContextResult>>`. Await at pop time. If not resolved yet, return null — do not block.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-136-- The pop is destructive: clears the cache entry after reading so stale data never accumulates.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-137-- Prefetch should also fire on first turn (even though it won't be consumed until turn 2).
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-139-### openclaw-honcho adoption
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-140-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:141:Move `session.context()` from `before_prompt_build` to a post-`agent_end` background task. Store result in `state.contextCache`. In `before_prompt_build`, read from cache instead of calling Honcho. If cache is empty (turn 1), inject nothing — the prompt is still valid without Honcho context on the first turn.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-142-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-143----
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-147-### Problem
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-148-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:149:Honcho's dialectic endpoint supports reasoning levels from `minimal` to `max`. A fixed level per tool wastes budget on simple queries and under-serves complex ones.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-150-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-151-### Pattern

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-270-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:271:## Spec: session naming strategies
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-272-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-273-### Problem
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-274-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:275:A single global session means every project shares the same Honcho context. Per-directory sessions provide isolation without requiring users to name sessions manually.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-276-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-277-### Strategies
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-278-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:279:| Strategy | Session key | When to use |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-280-|---|---|---|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:281:| `per-directory` | basename of CWD | Default. Each project gets its own session. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:282:| `global` | fixed string `"global"` | Single cross-project session. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:283:| manual map | user-configured per path | `sessions` config map overrides directory basename. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:284:| title-based | sanitized session title | When agent supports named sessions set mid-conversation. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-285-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md-286-### Config schema

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:291:  "sessionPeerPrefix": false,

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.md:314:When a user asks "how do I change my memory settings?" the agent either hallucinates or says it doesn't know. The agent should know its own management interface.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-2-sidebar_position: 4
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:3:title: "Toolsets Reference"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:4:description: "Reference for Hermes core, composite, platform, and dynamic toolsets"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-5----
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-6-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:7:# Toolsets Reference
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-8-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:9:Toolsets are named bundles of tools that control what the agent can do. They're the primary mechanism for configuring tool availability per platform, per session, or per task.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-10-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:11:## How Toolsets Work
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-12-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:13:Every tool belongs to exactly one toolset. When you enable a toolset, all tools in that bundle become available to the agent. Toolsets come in three kinds:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-14-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:15:- **Core** — A single logical group of related tools (e.g., `file` bundles `read_file`, `write_file`, `patch`, `search_files`)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:16:- **Composite** — Combines multiple core toolsets for a common scenario (e.g., `debugging` bundles file, terminal, and web tools)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:17:- **Platform** — A complete tool configuration for a specific deployment context (e.g., `hermes-cli` is the default for interactive CLI sessions)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-18-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:19:## Configuring Toolsets
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-20-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:21:### Per-session (CLI)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-22-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:23:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:24:hermes chat --toolsets web,file,terminal
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:25:hermes chat --toolsets debugging        # composite — expands to file + terminal + web
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:26:hermes chat --toolsets all              # everything
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-27-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-28-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-30-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-31-```yaml
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:32:toolsets:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-33-  - hermes-cli          # default for CLI
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-34-  # - hermes-telegram   # override for Telegram gateway

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:40:hermes tools                            # curses UI to enable/disable per platform
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-41-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-42-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:43:Or in-session:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-44-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-45-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:46:/tools list
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:47:/tools disable browser

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-50-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:51:## Core Toolsets
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-52-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:53:| Toolset | Tools | Purpose |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-54-|---------|-------|---------|
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:55:| `browser` | `browser_back`, `browser_click`, `browser_console`, `browser_get_images`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_press`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_type`, `browser_vision`, `web_search` | Full browser automation. Includes `web_search` as a fallback for quick lookups. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-56-| `clarify` | `clarify` | Ask the user a question when the agent needs clarification. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:57:| `code_execution` | `execute_code` | Run Python scripts that call Hermes tools programmatically. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-58-| `cronjob` | `cronjob` | Schedule and manage recurring tasks. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:59:| `delegation` | `delegate_task` | Spawn isolated subagent instances for parallel work. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:60:| `file` | `patch`, `read_file`, `search_files`, `write_file` | File reading, writing, searching, and editing. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-61-| `homeassistant` | `ha_call_service`, `ha_get_state`, `ha_list_entities`, `ha_list_services` | Smart home control via Home Assistant. Only available when `HASS_TOKEN` is set. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-62-| `image_gen` | `image_generate` | Text-to-image generation via FAL.ai. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:63:| `memory` | `memory` | Persistent cross-session memory management. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:64:| `messaging` | `send_message` | Send messages to other platforms (Telegram, Discord, etc.) from within a session. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-65-| `moa` | `mixture_of_agents` | Multi-model consensus via Mixture of Agents. |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:66:| `rl` | `rl_check_status`, `rl_edit_config`, `rl_get_current_config`, `rl_get_results`, `rl_list_environments`, `rl_list_runs`, `rl_select_environment`, `rl_start_training`, `rl_stop_training`, `rl_test_inference` | RL training environment management (Atropos). |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:67:| `search` | `web_search` | Web search only (without extract). |

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:154:## Relationship to `hermes tools`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-155-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md:156:The `hermes tools` command provides a curses-based UI for toggling individual tools on or off per platform. This operates at the tool level (finer than toolsets) and persists to `config.yaml`. Disabled tools are filtered out even if their toolset is enabled.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md-157-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md-1-# Container-Aware CLI Review Fixes Spec
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md-2-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md:3:**PR:** NousResearch/hermes-agent#7543
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md-4-**Review:** cursor[bot] bugbot review (4094049442) + two prior rounds
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md-5-**Date:** 2026-04-12
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md-30-2. **No retries.** Probe once for sudo, exec once. If it fails, docker/podman's stderr reaches the user verbatim.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md-31-3. **Completely transparent.** No error wrapping, no prefixes, no spinners. Docker's output goes straight through.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md:32:4. **`os.execvp` on the happy path.** Replace the Python process entirely so there's no idle parent during interactive sessions. Note: `execvp` never returns on success (process is replaced) and raises `OSError` on failure (it does not return a value). The container process's exit code becomes the process exit code by definition — no explicit propagation needed.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md-33-5. **One human-readable exception to "let it crash".** `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` from the sudo probe gets a specific catch with a readable message, since a raw traceback for "your Docker daemon is slow" is confusing. All other exceptions propagate naturally.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/specs/container-cli-review-fixes.md-34-
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-39-### Does it work on Android / Termux?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-40-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:41:Yes — Hermes now has a tested Termux install path for Android phones.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-42-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-48-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-49-For the fully explicit manual steps, supported extras, and current limitations, see the [Termux guide](../getting-started/termux.md).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-50-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:51:Important caveat: the full `.[all]` extra is not currently available on Android because the `voice` extra depends on `faster-whisper` → `ctranslate2`, and `ctranslate2` does not publish Android wheels. Use the tested `.[termux]` extra instead.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-52-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-53-### Is my data sent anywhere?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-54-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:55:API calls go **only to the LLM provider you configure** (e.g., OpenRouter, your local Ollama instance). Hermes Agent does not collect telemetry, usage data, or analytics. Your conversations, memory, and skills are stored locally in `~/.hermes/`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-56-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-57-### Can I use it offline / with local models?
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:61:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-62-hermes model

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-66-# Model name: qwen3.5:27b
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:67:# Context length: 32768   ← set this to match your server's actual context window

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-69-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-82-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-83-:::tip Ollama users
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:84:If you set a custom `num_ctx` in Ollama (e.g., `ollama run --num_ctx 16384`), make sure to set the matching context length in Hermes — Ollama's `/api/show` reports the model's *maximum* context, not the effective `num_ctx` you configured.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-85-:::
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-86-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-87-:::tip Timeouts with local models
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:88:Hermes auto-detects local endpoints and relaxes streaming timeouts (read timeout raised from 120s to 1800s, stale stream detection disabled). If you still hit timeouts on very large contexts, set `HERMES_STREAM_READ_TIMEOUT=1800` in your `.env`. See the [Local LLM guide](../guides/local-llm-on-mac.md#timeouts) for details.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-89-:::
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-90-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-97-Yes. The [messaging gateway](../user-guide/messaging/index.md) lets multiple users interact with the same Hermes Agent instance via Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, or Home Assistant. Access is controlled through allowlists (specific user IDs) and DM pairing (first user to message claims access).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-98-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:99:### What's the difference between memory and skills?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-100-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:101:- **Memory** stores **facts** — things the agent knows about you, your projects, and preferences. Memories are retrieved automatically based on relevance.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-102-- **Skills** store **procedures** — step-by-step instructions for how to do things. Skills are recalled when the agent encounters a similar task.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-103-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:104:Both persist across sessions. See [Memory](../user-guide/features/memory.md) and [Skills](../user-guide/features/skills.md) for details.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-105-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-106-### Can I use it in my own Python project?

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-125-#### `hermes: command not found` after installation

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-236-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:237:**Cause:** The conversation has grown too long for the model's context window, or Hermes detected the wrong context length for your model.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-238-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-239-**Solution:**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:240:```bash

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-243-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:244:# Or start a fresh session
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-245-hermes chat
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-246-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-249-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-250-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:251:If this happens on the first long conversation, Hermes may have the wrong context length for your model. Check what it detected:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-252-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:253:Look at the CLI startup line — it shows the detected context length (e.g., `📊 Context limit: 128000 tokens`). You can also check with `/usage` during a session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-254-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:255:To fix context detection, set it explicitly:

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-262-```

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-413-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:414:#### macOS: Node.js / ffmpeg / other tools not found by gateway
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-415-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:416:**Cause:** launchd services inherit a minimal PATH (`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`) that doesn't include Homebrew, nvm, cargo, or other user-installed tool directories. This commonly breaks the WhatsApp bridge (`node not found`) or voice transcription (`ffmpeg not found`).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-417-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:418:**Solution:** The gateway captures your shell PATH when you run `hermes gateway install`. If you installed tools after setting up the gateway, re-run the install to capture the updated PATH:

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-422-hermes gateway start      # Detects the updated plist and reloads
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-423-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-424-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:425:You can verify the plist has the correct PATH:
