runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-548-### How do profiles differ from just setting HERMES_HOME?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-549-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:550:Profiles are a managed layer on top of `HERMES_HOME`. You *could* manually set `HERMES_HOME=/some/path` before every command, but profiles handle all the plumbing for you: creating the directory structure, generating shell aliases (`hermes-work`), tracking the active profile in `~/.hermes/active_profile`, and syncing skill updates across all profiles automatically. They also integrate with tab completion so you don't have to remember paths.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-551-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-552-### Can two profiles share the same bot token?
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-554-No. Each messaging platform (Telegram, Discord, etc.) requires exclusive access to a bot token. If two profiles try to use the same token simultaneously, the second gateway will fail to connect. Create a separate bot per profile — for Telegram, talk to [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) to make additional bots.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-555-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:556:### Do profiles share memory or sessions?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-557-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:558:No. Each profile has its own memory store, session database, and skills directory. They are completely isolated. If you want to start a new profile with existing memories and sessions, use `hermes profile create newname --clone-all` to copy everything from the current profile.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-559-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-560-### What happens when I run `hermes update`?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-561-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:562:`hermes update` pulls the latest code and reinstalls dependencies **once** (not per-profile). It then syncs updated skills to all profiles automatically. You only need to run `hermes update` once — it covers every profile on the machine.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-563-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-564-### Can I move a profile to a different machine?
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-566-Yes. Export the profile to a portable archive and import it on the other machine:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-567-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:568:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-569-# On the source machine
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-570-hermes profile export work ./work-backup.tar.gz
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-574-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-575-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:576:The imported profile will have all config, memories, sessions, and skills from the export. You may need to update paths or re-authenticate with providers if the new machine has a different setup.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-577-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-578-### How many profiles can I run?
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-588-**Scenario:** You use GPT-5.4 as your daily driver, but Gemini or Grok writes better social media content. Manually switching models every time is tedious.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-589-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:590:**Solution: Delegation config.** Hermes can route subagents to a different model automatically. Set this in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-591-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-592-```yaml
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-593-delegation:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:594:  model: "google/gemini-3-flash-preview"   # subagents use this model
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:595:  provider: "openrouter"                    # provider for subagents
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-596-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-597-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:598:Now when you tell Hermes "write me a Twitter thread about X" and it spawns a `delegate_task` subagent, that subagent runs on Gemini instead of your main model. Your primary conversation stays on GPT-5.4.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-599-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:600:You can also be explicit in your prompt: *"Delegate a task to write social media posts about our product launch. Use your subagent for the actual writing."* The agent will use `delegate_task`, which automatically picks up the delegation config.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-601-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-602-For one-off model switches without delegation, use `/model` in the CLI:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-603-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:604:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:605:/model google/gemini-3-flash-preview    # switch for this session
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-606-# ... write your content ...
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-607-/model openai/gpt-5.4                   # switch back
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-608-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-609-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:610:See [Subagent Delegation](../user-guide/features/delegation.md) for more on how delegation works.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-611-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-612-### Running multiple agents on one WhatsApp number (per-chat binding)
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-614-**Scenario:** In OpenClaw, you had multiple independent agents bound to specific WhatsApp chats — one for a family shopping list group, another for your private chat. Can Hermes do this?
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-615-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:616:**Current limitation:** Hermes profiles each require their own WhatsApp number/session. You cannot bind multiple profiles to different chats on the same WhatsApp number — the WhatsApp bridge (Baileys) uses one authenticated session per number.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-617-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-618-**Workarounds:**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-619-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:620:1. **Use a single profile with personality switching.** Create different `AGENTS.md` context files or use the `/personality` command to change behavior per chat. The agent sees which chat it's in and can adapt.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-621-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-622-2. **Use cron jobs for specialized tasks.** For a shopping list tracker, set up a cron job that monitors a specific chat and manages the list — no separate agent needed.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-624-3. **Use separate numbers.** If you need truly independent agents, pair each profile with its own WhatsApp number. Virtual numbers from services like Google Voice work for this.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-625-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:626:4. **Use Telegram or Discord instead.** These platforms support per-chat binding more naturally — each Telegram group or Discord channel gets its own session, and you can run multiple bot tokens (one per profile) on the same account.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-627-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-628-See [Profiles](../user-guide/profiles.md) and [WhatsApp setup](../user-guide/messaging/whatsapp.md) for more details.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-630-### Controlling what shows up in Telegram (hiding logs and reasoning)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-631-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:632:**Scenario:** You see gateway exec logs, Hermes reasoning, and tool call details in Telegram instead of just the final output.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-633-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:634:**Solution:** The `display.tool_progress` setting in `config.yaml` controls how much tool activity is shown:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-635-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-636-```yaml
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-637-display:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:638:  tool_progress: "off"   # options: off, new, all, verbose
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-639-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-640-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:641:- **`off`** — Only the final response. No tool calls, no reasoning, no logs.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:642:- **`new`** — Shows new tool calls as they happen (brief one-liners).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:643:- **`all`** — Shows all tool activity including results.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:644:- **`verbose`** — Full detail including tool arguments and outputs.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-645-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-646-For messaging platforms, `off` or `new` is usually what you want. After editing `config.yaml`, restart the gateway for changes to take effect.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-647-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:648:You can also toggle this per-session with the `/verbose` command (if enabled):
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-649-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-650-```yaml
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-651-display:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:652:  tool_progress_command: true   # enables /verbose in the gateway
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-653-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-654-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-672-:::
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-673-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:674:### Shared thread sessions (multiple users, one conversation)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-675-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:676:**Scenario:** You have a Telegram or Discord thread where multiple people mention the bot. You want all mentions in that thread to be part of one shared conversation, not separate per-user sessions.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-677-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:678:**Current behavior:** Hermes creates sessions keyed by user ID on most platforms, so each person gets their own conversation context. This is by design for privacy and context isolation.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-679-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-680-**Workarounds:**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-681-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:682:1. **Use Slack.** Slack sessions are keyed by thread, not by user. Multiple users in the same thread share one conversation — exactly the behavior you're describing. This is the most natural fit.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-683-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:684:2. **Use a group chat with a single user.** If one person is the designated "operator" who relays questions, the session stays unified. Others can read along.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-685-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:686:3. **Use a Discord channel.** Discord sessions are keyed by channel, so all users in the same channel share context. Use a dedicated channel for the shared conversation.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-687-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-688-### Exporting Hermes to another machine
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-693-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-694-1. Install Hermes Agent on the new machine:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:695:   ```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:696:   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-697-   ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-698-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-699-2. Copy your entire `~/.hermes/` directory **except** the `hermes-agent` subdirectory (that's the code repo — the new install has its own):
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:700:   ```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-701-   # On the source machine
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-702-   rsync -av --exclude='hermes-agent' ~/.hermes/ newmachine:~/.hermes/
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-704-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-705-   Or use profile export/import:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:706:   ```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-707-   # On source machine
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-708-   hermes profile export default ./hermes-backup.tar.gz
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-712-   ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-713-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:714:3. On the new machine, run `hermes setup` to verify API keys and provider config are working. Re-authenticate any messaging platforms (especially WhatsApp, which uses QR pairing).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-715-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:716:The `~/.hermes/` directory contains everything: `config.yaml`, `.env`, `SOUL.md`, `memories/`, `skills/`, `state.db` (sessions), `cron/`, and any custom plugins. The code itself lives in `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/` and is installed fresh.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-717-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:718:### Permission denied when reloading shell after install
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-719-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-720-**Scenario:** After running the Hermes installer, `source ~/.zshrc` gives a permission denied error.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-721-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:722:**Cause:** This usually happens when `~/.zshrc` (or `~/.bashrc`) has incorrect file permissions, or when the installer couldn't write to it cleanly. It's not a Hermes-specific issue — it's a shell config permissions problem.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-723-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-724-**Solution:**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:725:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-726-# Check permissions
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-727-ls -la ~/.zshrc
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-737-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-738-If the installer added the PATH line but permissions are wrong, you can add it manually:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:739:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-740-echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-741-```
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-748-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-749-**Solution:**
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:750:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-751-# Check what model and provider are configured
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-752-hermes config show | head -20
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-755-hermes model
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-756-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:757:# Or test with a known-good model
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-758-hermes chat -q "hello" --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-759-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-760-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:761:If using OpenRouter, make sure your API key has credits. A 400 from OpenRouter often means the model requires a paid plan or the model ID has a typo.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-762-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-763----
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-767-If your issue isn't covered here:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-768-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:769:1. **Search existing issues:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md:770:2. **Ask the community:** [Nous Research Discord](https://discord.gg/nousresearch)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/website/docs/reference/faq.md-771-3. **File a bug report:** Include your OS, Python version (`python3 --version`), Hermes version (`hermes --version`), and the full error message

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-189-  <h2>Overview</h2>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-190-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:191:  <p>Two independent Honcho integrations have been built for two different agent runtimes: <strong>Hermes Agent</strong> (Python, baked into the runner) and <strong>openclaw-honcho</strong> (TypeScript plugin via hook/tool API). Both use the same Honcho peer paradigm — dual peer model, <code>session.context()</code>, <code>peer.chat()</code> — but they made different tradeoffs at every layer.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-192-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-193-  <p>This document maps those tradeoffs and defines a porting spec: a set of Hermes-originated patterns, each stated as an integration-agnostic interface, that any Honcho integration can adopt regardless of runtime or language.</p>
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-203-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-204-  <h3>Hermes: baked-in runner</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:205:  <p>Honcho is initialised directly inside <code>AIAgent.__init__</code>. There is no plugin boundary. Session management, context injection, async prefetch, and CLI surface are all first-class concerns of the runner. Context is injected once per session (baked into <code>_cached_system_prompt</code>) and never re-fetched mid-session — this maximises prefix cache hits at the LLM provider.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-206-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-207-  <div class="mermaid">
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-213-    LLM --> R["response"]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-214-    R --> FP["_honcho_fire_prefetch()<br/>(daemon threads, turn end)"]
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:215:    FP --> C1["prefetch_context() thread"]

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-230-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-231-  <h3>openclaw-honcho: hook-based plugin</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:232:  <p>The plugin registers hooks against OpenClaw's event bus. Context is fetched synchronously inside <code>before_prompt_build</code> on every turn. Message capture happens in <code>agent_end</code>. The multi-agent hierarchy is tracked via <code>subagent_spawned</code>. This model is correct but every turn pays a blocking Honcho round-trip before the LLM call can begin.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-233-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-395-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-396-  <h3>Problem</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:397:  <p>Calling <code>session.context()</code> and <code>peer.chat()</code> synchronously before each LLM call adds 200–800ms of Honcho round-trip latency to every turn. Users experience this as the agent "thinking slowly."</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-398-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-399-  <h3>Pattern</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:400:  <p>Fire both calls as non-blocking background work at the <strong>end</strong> of each turn. Store results in a per-session cache keyed by session ID. At the <strong>start</strong> of the next turn, pop from cache — the HTTP is already done. First turn is cold (empty cache); all subsequent turns are zero-latency on the response path.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-401-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-402-  <h3>Interface contract</h3>
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-404-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-405-<span class="kw">interface</span> <span class="key">AsyncPrefetch</span> {
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:406:  <span class="cm">// Fire context + dialectic fetches at turn end. Non-blocking.</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:407:  firePrefetch(sessionId: <span class="str">string</span>, userMessage: <span class="str">string</span>): <span class="kw">void</span>;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-408-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-409-  <span class="cm">// Pop cached results at turn start. Returns empty if cache is cold.</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:410:  popContextResult(sessionId: <span class="str">string</span>): ContextResult | <span class="kw">null</span>;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:411:  popDialecticResult(sessionId: <span class="str">string</span>): <span class="str">string</span> | <span class="kw">null</span>;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-412-}
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-413-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:414:<span class="kw">type</span> <span class="key">ContextResult</span> = {
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-415-  representation: <span class="str">string</span>;
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-416-  card: <span class="str">string</span>[];
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:417:  aiRepresentation?: <span class="str">string</span>;  <span class="cm">// AI peer context if enabled</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-418-  summary?: <span class="str">string</span>;            <span class="cm">// conversation summary if fetched</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-419-};</code></pre>
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-421-  <h3>Implementation notes</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-422-  <ul>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:423:    <li>Python: <code>threading.Thread(daemon=True)</code>. Write to <code>dict[session_id, result]</code> — GIL makes this safe for simple writes.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:424:    <li>TypeScript: <code>Promise</code> stored in <code>Map&lt;string, Promise&lt;ContextResult&gt;&gt;</code>. Await at pop time. If not resolved yet, skip (return null) — do not block.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-425-    <li>The pop is destructive: clears the cache entry after reading so stale data never accumulates.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-426-    <li>Prefetch should also fire on first turn (even though it won't be consumed until turn 2) — this ensures turn 2 is never cold.</li>
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-428-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-429-  <h3>openclaw-honcho adoption</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:430:  <p>Move <code>session.context()</code> from <code>before_prompt_build</code> to a post-<code>agent_end</code> background task. Store result in <code>state.contextCache</code>. In <code>before_prompt_build</code>, read from cache instead of calling Honcho. If cache is empty (turn 1), inject nothing — the prompt is still valid without Honcho context on the first turn.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-431-</section>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-432-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-436-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-437-  <h3>Problem</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:438:  <p>Honcho's dialectic endpoint supports reasoning levels from <code>minimal</code> to <code>max</code>. A fixed level per tool wastes budget on simple queries and under-serves complex ones.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-439-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-440-  <h3>Pattern</h3>
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-463-</section>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-464-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:465:<!-- SPEC: PER-PEER MEMORY MODES -->
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-466-<section id="spec-modes">
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:467:  <h2>Spec: per-peer memory modes</h2>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-468-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-469-  <h3>Problem</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:470:  <p>Users want independent control over whether user context and agent context are written locally, to Honcho, or both. A single <code>memoryMode</code> shorthand is not granular enough.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-471-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-472-  <h3>Pattern</h3>
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-480-      <span class="str">"config"</span>: {
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-481-        <span class="str">"apiKey"</span>: <span class="str">"..."</span>,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:482:        <span class="str">"memoryMode"</span>: <span class="str">"hybrid"</span>,          <span class="cm">// shorthand: both peers</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:483:        <span class="str">"userMemoryMode"</span>: <span class="str">"honcho"</span>,       <span class="cm">// override for user peer</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:484:        <span class="str">"agentMemoryMode"</span>: <span class="str">"hybrid"</span>       <span class="cm">// override for agent peer</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-485-      }
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-486-    }
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-490-  <h3>Resolution order</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-491-  <ol>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:492:    <li>Per-peer field (<code>userMemoryMode</code> / <code>agentMemoryMode</code>) — wins if present.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:493:    <li>Shorthand <code>memoryMode</code> — applies to both peers as default.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-494-    <li>Hardcoded default: <code>"hybrid"</code>.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-495-  </ol>
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-497-  <h3>Effect on Honcho sync</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-498-  <ul>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:499:    <li><code>userMemoryMode=local</code>: skip adding user peer messages to Honcho.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:500:    <li><code>agentMemoryMode=local</code>: skip adding assistant peer messages to Honcho.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:501:    <li>Both local: skip <code>session.addMessages()</code> entirely.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:502:    <li><code>userMemoryMode=honcho</code>: disable local USER.md writes.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:503:    <li><code>agentMemoryMode=honcho</code>: disable local MEMORY.md / SOUL.md writes.</li>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-504-  </ul>

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-543-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-544-  <h3>Part C: migrate agent files at setup</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:545:  <p>During <code>openclaw honcho setup</code>, upload agent-self files (SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, AGENTS.md, BOOTSTRAP.md) to the agent peer using <code>seedAiIdentity()</code> instead of <code>session.uploadFile()</code>. This routes the content through Honcho's observation pipeline rather than the file store.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-546-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:563:<!-- SPEC: SESSION NAMING -->
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:564:<section id="spec-sessions">
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:565:  <h2>Spec: session naming strategies</h2>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-566-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-567-  <h3>Problem</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:568:  <p>When Honcho is used across multiple projects or directories, a single global session means every project shares the same context. Per-directory sessions provide isolation without requiring users to name sessions manually.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-569-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-570-  <h3>Strategies</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-571-  <div class="table-wrap">
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-572-    <table>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:573:      <thead><tr><th>Strategy</th><th>Session key</th><th>When to use</th></tr></thead>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-574-      <tbody>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:575:        <tr><td><code>per-directory</code></td><td>basename of CWD</td><td>Default. Each project gets its own session.</td></tr>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:576:        <tr><td><code>global</code></td><td>fixed string <code>"global"</code></td><td>Single cross-project session.</td></tr>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:577:        <tr><td>manual map</td><td>user-configured per path</td><td><code>sessions</code> config map overrides directory basename.</td></tr>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:578:        <tr><td>title-based</td><td>sanitized session title</td><td>When agent supports named sessions; title set mid-conversation.</td></tr>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-579-      </tbody>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-580-    </table>
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-583-  <h3>Config schema</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-584-  <pre><code>{
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:585:  <span class="str">"sessionStrategy"</span>: <span class="str">"per-directory"</span>,   <span class="cm">// "per-directory" | "global"</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:586:  <span class="str">"sessionPeerPrefix"</span>: <span class="kw">false</span>,            <span class="cm">// prepend peer name to session key</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:587:  <span class="str">"sessions"</span>: {                            <span class="cm">// manual overrides</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-588-    <span class="str">"/home/user/projects/foo"</span>: <span class="str">"foo-project"</span>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-589-  }

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-598-</section>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-599-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-603-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-604-  <h3>Problem</h3>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:605:  <p>When a user asks "how do I change my memory settings?" or "what Honcho commands are available?" the agent either hallucinates or says it doesn't know. The agent should know its own management interface.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-606-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html:608:  <p>When Honcho is active, append a compact command reference to the system prompt. The agent can cite these commands directly instead of guessing.</p>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/hermes-docs/docs/honcho-integration-spec.html-609-
